self.description: A numeric Series with no missing values
self.constraints: st.lists(st.floats(allow_nan=False, allow_infinity=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6), min_size=1, max_size=10).map(lambda x: pd.Series(x, dtype=float))

self.description: A numeric Series with some NaN values
self.constraints: st.lists(st.one_of(st.floats(allow_nan=False, allow_infinity=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6), st.just(float('nan'))), min_size=1, max_size=10).map(lambda x: pd.Series(x, dtype=float))

self.description: A numeric Series with a string index
self.constraints: st.fixed_dictionaries({'a': st.floats(allow_nan=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6), 'b': st.floats(allow_nan=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6), 'c': st.floats(allow_nan=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6)}).map(lambda d: pd.Series(d))

other.description: Series with identical index to self
other.constraints: st.lists(st.floats(allow_nan=False, allow_infinity=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6), min_size=1, max_size=10).map(lambda x: pd.Series(x, dtype=float))

other.description: Series with partially overlapping index (alignment needed)
other.constraints: st.fixed_dictionaries({'a': st.floats(allow_nan=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6), 'd': st.floats(allow_nan=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6)}).map(lambda d: pd.Series(d))
st.lists(st.one_of(st.floats(allow_nan=False, allow_infinity=False, min_value=-1e6, max_value=1e6), st.just(float('nan'))), min_size=1, max_size=10).map(lambda x: pd.Series(x, dtype=float))

fill_value.description: fill_value=None (NaN) — default; missing fills remain NaN
fill_value=0 — fill missing with 0 before multiplication

axis.description: axis=0 or 'index' — only valid values per doc

post_condition.source: Returns: Series — The result of the operation.

post_condition.expected_behavior: assert all(result[i] == self.iloc[i] * other.iloc[i] for i in range(len(self)))

post_condition.source: Fill existing missing (NaN) values, and any new element needed for successful Series alignment, with this value before computation.
If data in both corresponding Series locations is missing the result of filling (at that location) will be missing.
any new element needed for successful Series alignment, with this value before computation
Fill existing missing (NaN) values, and any new element needed for successful Series alignment, with this value before computation. >>> a.mul(5, fill_value=0) — d    0.0

post_condition.implicit_reason: Element-wise scalar multiplication cannot change the number of elements; follows logically from the definition of element-wise operations.
Scalar multiplication does not change alignment; the output index must match the input Series index.
Any finite number multiplied by zero equals zero; follows from basic arithmetic applied element-wise.

post_condition.source: See also: Series.rmul — Reverse of the Multiplication operator
post_condition.implicit_reason: Multiplication is commutative; mul and rmul with the same inputs should yield the same result for scalars.
